title: Knowledge grounding: which data can a Copilot Studio agent answer from?
summary: The documented controls, knowledge-source behavior and quoted billing rates are supported by Microsoft's current pages. Minor corrections should complete the Dataverse search path, clarify the Microsoft 365 channel qualification for included usage and add supporting source links.

claims.claim: Knowledge grounding points an agent at content to ground its answers.
claims.quote: Knowledge sources ground your agent's responses in enterprise data.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio calls these enterprise-data grounding inputs knowledge sources.
claims.quote: When you add knowledge sources, agents can use enterprise data from Power Platform, Dynamics 365 data, websites, and external systems.

claims.claim: Standard-harness makers can add knowledge on the agent's Knowledge page.
claims.quote: You can incorporate knowledge at the agent level, in the **Knowledge** page

claims.claim: Knowledge can also be added in a generative answers node inside an agent topic.
claims.quote: or at the topic level, with a [generative answers node](nlu-boost-node) in an agent topic.

claims.claim: A published agent uses its configured knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Published agents that contain knowledge use the configured knowledge sources to ground the published agent.

claims.quote: You can add up to 15 Dataverse tables per knowledge source.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: maker choices
claims.claim: Makers choose the knowledge sources configured for their agents.

claims.claim: Administrators can restrict the types of knowledge sources available to agents.
claims.quote: The **Knowledge sources for agents** setting controls access to sources like SharePoint, public websites, and documents such as files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: default
claims.claim: The Knowledge sources for agents preview page does not state the setting's default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Allow ungrounded responses permits general-knowledge answers without a knowledge source or tool.
claims.quote: When you turn on the **Allow ungrounded responses** setting, your agent can respond by using the model's general knowledge, even when it doesn't use any knowledge sources or tools.

claims.claim: No admin-centre setting for Allow ungrounded responses is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow ungrounded responses" "admin" and "Allow ungrounded responses" admin API Dataverse bot configuration PowerShell; opened Knowledge sources summary and Agent (bot) reference. No admin-centre equivalent found.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits meter grounded-answer usage.
claims.quote: *Copilot Credits* are the unit that measures agent usage.

claims.claim: The cited Billing rates and management page describes standard-harness agents.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the [standard harness](harnesses-overview#standard-harness).

claims.claim: The standard-harness Classic answer rate is 1 Copilot Credit.
claims.quote: | Classic answer | 1 Copilot Credit | No charge |

claims.claim: The standard-harness Generative answer feature rate is 2 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Generative answer^2^ | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Tenant graph grounding
claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding for messages has a rate of 10 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Tenant graph grounding for messages | 10 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: Microsoft illustrates a complex tenant-graph-grounded prompt using 12 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 Copilot Credits (10 Copilot Credits for tenant graph grounding, and 2 Copilot Credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing also charges for the harness itself.
claims.quote: and the harness itself. Any experience that uses one of these consumes credits.

claims.claim: Included employee-facing usage requires operation under the authenticated licensed user's identity.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Agent Builder exception
claims.claim: The billing page says generative answers incur charges unless created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 without tenant graph grounding.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: optional tenant graph grounding
claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding can be turned on or off for each agent.
claims.quote: This capability is optional, and you can turn it on or off for each agent.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph default
claims.claim: Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences use tenant graph grounding semantic search by default.
claims.quote: By default, all users with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses use tenant graph grounding semantic search.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[4].governs; What to check
claims.claim: Enabling tenant graph grounding for users without Microsoft 365 Copilot licences adds cost.
claims.quote: if not all end users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, turn on this setting to leverage semantic index for those users to improve quality. This feature comes at an extra cost.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding requires a configured semantic index.
claims.quote: It also requires that a semantic index is configured for use.

claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence must be assigned to at least one user in the agent's tenant.
claims.quote: This feature requires the agent to share a tenant with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. It also requires that a semantic index is configured for use. To use a semantic index, the Microsoft 365 Copilot license must be assigned to at least one user in the enterprise.

claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: When you use **Upload files > SharePoint** as a knowledge source, your files are stored in Dataverse, where they're processed and indexed for use.

claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint consume Dataverse data storage.
claims.quote: Your files and folders remain in Dataverse, so they do consume data storage.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers stay possible
claims.claim: Turning off Allow ungrounded responses does not prevent combining general knowledge with retrieved content.
claims.quote: The agent's underlying model might still incorporate general knowledge when it combines this knowledge with information it retrieves from knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: Turning off Allow ungrounded responses blocks responses from turns that used no knowledge source or tool.
claims.quote: When you turn off this setting, the agent blocks any response generated in a turn where it didn't use a knowledge source or tool.

claims.claim: A follow-up answered only from conversation history can be blocked.
claims.quote: the response is blocked if the agent answers a question from conversation history or general knowledge without calling a knowledge source or tool.

claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses off, knowledge-source answers require an in-text source citation.
claims.quote: When you turn off **Allow ungrounded responses**, the agent returns an answer from a knowledge source only when the answer includes an in-text citation to that source.

claims.where: Risks and limits: correct uncited answers
claims.claim: The agent withholds a correct knowledge-source answer if it lacks a citation.
claims.quote: Occasionally, the model generates a correct answer from a knowledge source but doesn't include a citation for it. When that happens, the agent withholds the answer and responds as though it didn't find any information.

claims.claim: Blocking Documents through the knowledge-source setting only prevents local file uploads.
claims.quote: Configuring **Documents** knowledge source to not allow uploads only prevents local file uploads.

claims.where: Risks and limits: SharePoint and OneDrive uploads
claims.claim: Blocking Documents does not block SharePoint or OneDrive uploads; those require restricting SharePoint + OneDrive.
claims.quote:
It doesn't prevent makers from adding files from SharePoint or OneDrive.

To not allow uploads from SharePoint or OneDrive, configure **SharePoint + OneDrive** to not allow access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Uploaded files skip per-user checks
claims.claim: The file upload method permits anyone with access to the agent to access uploaded content.
claims.quote: The upload files method allows anyone with permission to the agent to access the file.

claims.claim: SharePoint sources verify the user's access credentials before answering.
claims.quote: With SharePoint, the user's credentials are verified to ensure they have permission to access the file before providing responses.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dataverse search; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft gives a 12-hour index-removal period after turning off Dataverse search, with a multi-day caveat.
claims.quote: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes the index within 12 hours.

claims.claim: Turning off Dataverse search prevents uploaded-file and OneDrive or SharePoint upload knowledge experiences from working.
claims.quote: can't use the search capability in the Power Apps navigation bar or any generative AI experience that relies on Dataverse, like uploaded files or using OneDrive or SharePoint files (via upload) in Microsoft Copilot Studio agents

claims.where: Risks and limits: rebuilding the search index
claims.claim: Rebuilding the Dataverse search index can take an hour or more for average-size organizations.
claims.quote: Syncing can take an hour or more for average size organizations

claims.where: Risks and limits: rebuilding the search index
claims.claim: A large organization's index rebuild can take a couple of days.
claims.quote: and a couple of days for large organizations.

claims.where: Risks and limits; What to check: multi-day caveat
claims.claim: Microsoft also cautions that index removal or provisioning can take multiple days depending on indexed volume.
claims.quote: Index removal (or provisioning) can take multiple days to be completed, depending on the amount of Dataverse search consumption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: standard-harness web search

claims.quote: It searches all public websites indexed by Bing.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding requires user authentication set to Authenticate with Microsoft.

claims.quote: Select either **Allow** or **Deny** under **Access** for each URL.

claims.quote:
**Yes**: Agents can use uploaded documents as knowledge sources.
